object_context: Fixed-cutoff/infinite-volume strong-coupling source-to-transfer gluing atom: bind Shen-Zhu-Zhu smooth gauge-invariant cylinder covariance decay to the same Osterwalder-Schrader physical Hilbert space and one-step transfer operator used by the abstract YM-S1a1 dense-source spectral exclusion lemma. Close only reflection-positivity inheritance, controlled-source density, and translated-covariance/time-distance interfaces. Do not claim RG transport, continuum scaling, continuum existence, novelty, or Clay-root authority.
structural_coordinates: SZZ finite-volume measures are Wilson plaquette Gibbs measures on SO(N) or SU(N) edge variables and converge under Assumption 1.1 to a unique infinite-volume measure.
SZZ Corollary 1.6 controls covariance for arbitrary disjoint-support smooth cylinder functions with one common exponent c_N at fixed strong-coupling parameters and source-dependent finite prefactors.

Luescher's OS construction builds the physical Hilbert space from gauge-invariant positive-time observables modulo null vectors and identifies one-step positive Euclidean-time translation with T=exp(-aH).
The SZZ Langevin/Markov generator gap is not the physical Hamiltonian gap and is excluded from the target bridge.
Finite-volume Wilson reflection positivity must be passed to the exact SZZ infinite-volume measure for the chosen reflection plane and local positive-time algebra.
The SZZ-controlled gauge-invariant smooth cylinder subalgebra must be dense in the same OS Hilbert completion; generic fixed-graph spin-network completeness is not sufficient.
Centered sources must be dense in the vacuum-orthogonal sector rather than merely dense including the vacuum.
For fixed finite source support, positive-time translation must give the exact OS transfer moment and support distance n+O_F(1) in SZZ's edge-support metric.
If S1a2 closes, the consequence is only a fixed-cutoff/infinite-volume/strong-coupling transfer spectral gap via the already-supported YM-S1a1 abstract lemma.
G5 RG transport, G6 physical lattice-spacing scaling, G7 continuum spectral identification, continuum existence/nontriviality and root assurance remain open.
equivalent_formulations: OS-form: show the unique SZZ infinite-volume measure is reflection positive on the local positive-time gauge-invariant algebra, reconstruct T, and prove the SZZ-controlled source images are dense in Omega-perp.

Approximation-form: show gauge-invariant smooth positive-time cylinders are dense in an ordinary L2(mu) source space and that the OS seminorm is continuously controlled by L2(mu), so their OS classes are dense after quotient/completion.
Moment-form: for centered F in the controlled dense class, identify Cov_mu(F,tau_n F)=<[F],T^n[F]> and transfer SZZ's exp(-c_N d) bound to one common nth-root ceiling q<1.
Geometry-form: prove d(Lambda_F,Lambda_tau_nF)=n+O_F(1) for fixed finite support in the chosen Euclidean time direction.
solved_analogues: YM-S1a1 abstract positive self-adjoint dense-source moment-to-spectral-support exclusion is already locally supported, with the q=0 target-facing logarithm boundary corrected in later history.
Luescher 1977 gives an explicit Wilson-lattice OS/transfer construction at finite volume from positive-time gauge-invariant observables.
SZZ prove unique infinite-volume convergence and a common exponential covariance rate over smooth cylinder functions in an explicit strong-coupling regime.
near_solved_analogues: For finite products of compact Lie groups, smooth functions are dense in L2 of finite-dimensional probability marginals; gauge averaging is a natural route to gauge-invariant approximants, but exact OS-support and norm details remain to be proved.

Reflection positivity inequalities for fixed local observables are closed under limits of their expectations, suggesting a short finite-volume-to-infinite-volume inheritance argument once boundary/reflection conventions are aligned.

method_transfers.source_context: Osterwalder-Schrader positive-time reconstruction for Wilson lattice gauge theory
method_transfers.method: Treat source completeness as density of the positive-time observable algebra in the reconstructed quotient/completion, not as an unrelated kinematic basis theorem.
required_assumptions: reflection plane compatible with source supports
infinite-volume expectation limits exist for the local products used in the OS form
disanalogies: Luescher's explicit construction is finite-volume/canonical while SZZ's target measure is an infinite-volume limit
OS algebra density does not automatically imply SZZ smooth-cylinder subclass density
method_transfers.repair_question: Can reflection positivity and one-step shift descend to the unique SZZ limit for every fixed local positive-time gauge-invariant source?

method_transfers.source_context: Smooth approximation on finite compact-group coordinate sets
method_transfers.method: Approximate positive-time gauge-invariant cylinder observables by smooth gauge-invariant cylinders in ordinary L2 and transfer the approximation through a bounded OS seminorm.
required_assumptions: finite-coordinate cylinders are dense in L2(mu)
smooth functions are dense for each finite marginal
OS seminorm is controlled by ordinary L2(mu) under reflection invariance
disanalogies: ordinary L2 convergence need not imply OS convergence without the norm comparison
centering/vacuum quotient must be handled explicitly
method_transfers.repair_question: Does the exact SZZ infinite-volume measure and reflection map provide the required L2-to-OS continuity and centered density?

method_transfers.source_context: SZZ Corollary 1.6 plus fixed-source Euclidean time translation
method_transfers.method: Use the common c_N exponent and fixed source-dependent prefactors to obtain one source-independent nth-root rate after proving support distance grows linearly in the time shift.
required_assumptions: translated source remains in the controlled class
supports are disjoint for large n
centered covariance equals the OS transfer moment
disanalogies: SZZ labels correlation decay a mass gap in statistical-mechanics language but does not by itself identify the physical transfer Hamiltonian
fixed strong coupling does not approach the four-dimensional continuum trajectory
method_transfers.repair_question: What exact centering and offset convention makes the SZZ covariance the T^n moment of the same OS source class?

explicit_disanalogies: Langevin-generator Poincare/log-Sobolev gap is not the physical transfer/Hamiltonian gap.
Exponential covariance decay without source density can miss a hidden lower-energy state.
Kinematic fixed-graph basis completeness is not density in the SZZ infinite-volume OS Hilbert space.
Ordinary L2 density is not OS density without a norm-continuity witness.
A fixed-cutoff strong-coupling gap does not imply a finite positive physical continuum mass gap.
